rv.q: "Dear Evan Hansen" is musical storytelling of the highest caliber, a work whose captivatingly generous spirit is matched by its exemplary intelligence and fearless embrace of deep feeling.
It’s the finest, most emotionally resonant score yet from this promising young songwriting team.
And not since "Next to Normal" has a score (by Benj Pask and Justin Paul) tapped so deeply into the psyches of its troubled characters.

That element of surprise is the most interesting thing about this overlong, self-satisfied show about campus sexuality and power games — and, fittingly, the production is staged in colleges around the city.
Dear Evan Hansen has only to embrace its potential bigness a little more.
Platt’s performance, and the emotions he draws out of the audience, lingers long after his final bow.

cn.t: Critics hail this Off-Broadway gem as musical storytelling of the highest caliber, with Ben Platt's remarkable performance and Pasek and Paul's deeply emotional score capturing teen anxiety and identity with humor, pathos, and fearless feeling.
